Fixed. In `middleware/proxy.go`, both balancers panicked when their target list was empty (`rand.Intn(0)` -> "invalid argument to Intn", and `% uint32(0)` -> divide by zero). Now:
- `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` return `nil` when there are no targets (also added the missing read lock in the round-robin variant).
- `ProxyWithConfig` checks for a nil target and returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) instead of dereferencing it.

Verified: a middleware using `NewRandomBalancer(nil)` / `NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)` now responds 503 with no panic, and the full suite (`go test ./...`, plus `-race` on the proxy tests) passes.

Working on the context.go Scheme bug: Scheme() currently returns raw X-Forwarded-Proto/Protocol/X-Url-Scheme values even when they are not valid schemes (the Context interface documents the return as `http` or `https`), so invalid header values must be ignored and the next header/fallback used. ETA ~12 min (also finishing the router.go item).
Starting on the bind.go bug (TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap / "ok, bind to map[string][]string") now. ETA ~20 min, after the context.go and router.go items.

Fixed in `context.go`: `Scheme()` returned raw header values even when they were not valid schemes, contradicting the `Context` interface contract ("Scheme returns the HTTP protocol scheme, `http` or `https`"). Now X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme are only used when they are `http` or `https`; otherwise the next header (or the `http` fallback) is used. Verified with the existing TestContext_Scheme plus subtests matching the two reported names (invalid X-Forwarded-Proto falls through to X-Forwarded-Protocol; all-invalid headers fall back to `http`).

Fixed in `bind.go`: `bindData` bound only `v[0]` for map destinations, so `map[string][]string` lost all but the first value of each key. Now, when the map's element type is a slice of strings, the whole value slice is bound (e.g. `?a=1&a=2` -> `map[string][]string{"a": {"1","2"}}`); other map element types keep the previous first-value behavior (and no longer panic for non-string element types). Verified with a local reproduction of TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap incl. the `ok, bind to map[string][]string` case; full suite still green.

Fixed in `middleware/compress.go`: an empty write (`c.String(200, "")`, `c.Blob(200, ct, []byte{})`, ...) reached the gzip writer, which emitted its 10-byte gzip header into the response while `Response.Size` stayed 0 — so the middleware removed `Content-Encoding` but left those 10 undecodable bytes in the body. `gzipResponseWriter.Write` now skips empty writes entirely, so an empty response stays empty (no Content-Encoding, no body bytes), consistent with the existing TestGzipNoContent expectations. Full suite still passes.

Status on the group.go item (TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware): I've reproduced a concrete defect — when two groups share the same path prefix, the second group's `Use` re-registers the `Any("", NotFoundHandler)` / `Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)` catch-all routes, which overwrite the first group's real route for that path (e.g. `g1.GET("", h)` then `g2 := e.Group("/group", m)` makes `GET /group` return 404 instead of running g1's handler). I'm finalizing the minimal fix in group.go and re-running the suite; ~3 min.

Fixed in `group.go`: `Group.Use` unconditionally re-registered the `""` and `"/*"` catch-all routes, so a second group sharing the same path prefix overwrote routes already registered for that path (e.g. `g1.GET("", h)` followed by `g2 := e.Group("/group", m)` made `GET /group` return 404 instead of g1's handler). `Use` now registers those catch-all routes only for methods/paths that are not already registered, so multiple groups with the same path keep their own routes and middleware. Verified with a local TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware reproduction; full suite still green.

Status on the router.go item (TestRouterNoRoutablePath): the router currently survives all the malformed/unroutable paths I fuzzed (no panic, no infinite loop, always a non-nil handler), so the defect is a subtler routing decision rather than a crash. I'm still narrowing it down (candidates: backtracking/`searchIndex` handling for `*`-only trees and the `MethodNotAllowedHandler` vs `NotFoundHandler` choice); ~3 min. All other reported bugs (proxy.go, context.go, bind.go, group.go, compress.go) are fixed and the whole suite is green.

router.go item not finished: the router does not crash or loop on the unroutable paths I fuzzed, so the defect is a subtler routing decision (backtracking/`searchIndex` state or the 404-vs-405 choice) that I could not pin down in the remaining time. Everything else reported is fixed and the full suite (`go test ./...`) passes: middleware/proxy.go (no-target balancer panic -> 503), context.go (Scheme ignores invalid forwarded schemes), bind.go (map[string][]string binding), group.go (same-path groups no longer overwrite each other's routes), middleware/compress.go (empty body no longer emits a stray gzip header).
